expectations.text: Names the connector and app developers as the hard side of this network
expectations.evidence: 'Hard side: the connector builders.'

expectations.text: States that the hard side determines whether the network survives and must be given a reason to build before customers see value
expectations.evidence: 'Customers will follow once connectors work'; first-party seeding gives day-one value.

expectations.text: Defines the atomic network as the smallest self-sustaining cluster - one use case, dense and mutually reinforcing
expectations.evidence: 'Atomic network: one use case, dense.'

expectations.text: Rejects the 60-connectors-across-every-category plan in favor of density over breadth, naming a broad thin catalog as the failure
expectations.evidence: 'Cut to a launch catalog of about 6-10 in one cluster... broad thin catalog'; 'expensive partner directory'.

expectations.text: Recommends first-party complements as the default seeding rung: the platform builds the first handful of connectors itself so day-one customers see value with no external dependency
expectations.evidence: 'First-party seeding (default rung)'.

expectations.text: Gives the promotion condition off first-party complements: when the catalog must outgrow what first-party engineering can build
expectations.evidence: No explicit condition is given for when the catalog outgrows first-party engineering.

expectations.text: Demotes the hackathon, stating that social mechanisms lose every efficiency round
expectations.evidence: 'Hackathons are the slowest seeding rung. They compound only on top of an existing community.'

expectations.text: Names the two conditions that would promote hackathons anyway: a compounding mandate plus an existing developer community
expectations.evidence: Only the community condition is stated. The compounding mandate is not given as a condition; compounding is merely assumed.

expectations.text: Notes that both hackathon promotion conditions fail here, citing the fixed four-month deadline and the absence of a developer community
expectations.evidence: Only the missing community is cited ('31 portal developers, no Discord'). The fixed deadline is not tied to a hackathon condition.

expectations.text: Notes that subsidies are promoted by a hard deadline only when real budget sits behind them, which is not yet the case here
expectations.evidence: 'A subsidy is promoted by a hard deadline with budget behind it. You have the deadline and no budget.'

expectations.text: Names the sequential / Trojan-horse option - ship a stand-alone tool the hard side wants on its own merits, 'come for the tool, stay for the network' - as the rung for a hard side with no reason to show up yet
expectations.evidence: 'connector template or SDK (the Trojan-horse tool, useful on its own)'.
